title: Calendar-day frame agreement — pin the frame, never pad the threshold
summary: Grounds decision #2985 (does the #670 born-active TTL need a grace day for operator timezone skew?). The survey corrects the card's premise: option 2 — compare in the operator's day rather than UTC — ALREADY SHIPPED in #2747's own resolve commit, and all four clock reads (check-standards.mjs, check-backlog-workflow.mjs, audit-backlog-health.mjs, and the dateScaffolded stamp itself) go through localToday(); on any single machine the skew is exactly zero. The card's cost claim is false for the same reason — workflow-invariants.cjs takes `today` as an injected argument and never reads a clock, so no CJS date helper is needed. What survives is a cross-MACHINE frame gap: the repo health gate also runs in CI, where GitHub-hosted runners are UTC and no workflow sets TZ or BACKLOG_TZ, so CI's 'today' and the operator's dateScaffolded are two different frames. Prior art is one-sided on the remedy. Temporal makes the zone an explicit argument (Temporal.Now.plainDateISO(timeZone) — one instant reads as two different 'todays'), RFC 9557 exists because a bare offset is not a zone, git stores an instant plus an offset used only for rendering, and Noda Time formalises that Instant->LocalDate is unambiguous while LocalDate->Instant is not. No citable source endorses padding a staleness threshold to absorb timezone skew — the uniform advice is to normalise the frame. Two corrections the sources forced: Temporal does NOT call a zone-free calendar date meaningless (PlainDate is a deliberate concept for birthdays and alarms; the zone binds only at 'what is today' and at instant crossings), and GitHub's contributions-graph timezone story is unsettled between two first-party sources and should not be cited. A threshold bump is the broken branch on three grounded counts: it tolerates the real second-day staleness it was protecting, it is not even sufficient (two calendar frames can differ by TWO days — UTC+14 vs UTC-12), and it pays globally for an artifact that is local to the machines where nobody reads the warning. Full grounding in reports/2026-08-17-calendar-day-frame-agreement.md.
